info.name: Glasspot API
info.description: Full test collection for the Glasspot pooled-money API (apps/backend). Flow: (1) register + verify two users (Primary admin, Member) in Auth, (2) create a pot and activate it, (3) contribute / add members / trigger payout or refund / close, in Pots. Money-moving endpoints require an Idempotency-Key header (auto-filled). Bearer token auth is set at the collection level from {{accessToken}}, which the Auth requests populate automatically via test scripts.

request.description: Basic liveness + DB connectivity check. No auth required.

item.name: Auth

request.description: Creates the account and emails a 6-digit verification code. Check the API server logs / mailer output (Mailtrap, console transport, etc.) for the code, then paste it into the otpCode variable before running Verify Email.

exec: pm.test("Register response", () => { throw new Error("Status " + pm.response.code + ": " + pm.response.text()); });

request.description: Paste the 6-digit code from the registration email into the otpCode environment variable, then send. Sets accessToken/refreshToken/userId on success.

exec: pm.test("Verify email response", () => { throw new Error("Status " + pm.response.code + ": " + pm.response.text()); });

exec: pm.test("Register response", () => { throw new Error("Status " + pm.response.code + ": " + pm.response.text()); });

request.description: purpose: signup_verification | login | password_reset. Always returns a generic 200 message regardless of whether the email exists. This variant re-sends the signup-verification code — errors if the account is already verified.
Re-sends a login OTP without going through POST /auth/login again. Same rate limiting (60s cooldown + 5/hour) as any other purpose, scoped per {userId, purpose}.

Sends a password_reset code. Note: as of this collection's writing there is no dedicated /auth/reset-password endpoint yet to consume this code with — this purpose exists in the schema/service but the full reset flow isn't wired up end-to-end. Kept here for when that endpoint lands.
Password check only — never returns tokens directly. Sets userId and unlocks the OTP step. Check email/logs for the login code, paste into otpCode, then run Verify Login OTP.

exec: pm.test("Login response", () => { throw new Error("Status " + pm.response.code + ": " + pm.response.text()); });

request.description: Completes login. Sets accessToken/refreshToken/userId.

exec: pm.test("Verify login OTP response", () => { throw new Error("Status " + pm.response.code + ": " + pm.response.text()); });

request.description: Exchanges the current refresh token for a new pair. No auth header needed — this is how a client recovers from an expired access token.

exec: pm.test("Refresh response", () => { throw new Error("Status " + pm.response.code + ": " + pm.response.text()); });

request.description: Sets the caller's default payout destination for refundType='admin' pots. accountNumber/bankCode are validated against Nomba's bank-lookup API — use real sandbox test values.
Revokes the caller's own session (identified via the bearer access token, not the body).

item.description: Register two accounts first (Primary + Member) — the Pots folder needs a second user to invite as a pot member. OTP codes are emailed; there's no way around pasting them in manually unless your dev environment logs OTPs to the console.

item.name: Pots
Create Pot (one per payout mode)

request.description: payoutMode='target_based': payout fires automatically once targetDate and/or targetAmount (inside payoutConfig) is met — purely rule-driven, no admin-manual-trigger option (that's manual mode's job instead, optionally with a fixed destination — see 'Create Pot — Manual (Fixed Destination)'). goalAmount here is a SEPARATE, display-only figure (e.g. a bigger publicly-stated goal than the actual trigger amount) — it never affects when payout fires. Sets potId on success.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Rent Contribution",
  "description": "Group pot to cover shared rent",
  "potType": "private",
  "refundType": "contributors",
  "minContribution": 100000,
  "maxContribution": 5000000,
  "goalAmount": 10000000,
  "payoutMode": "target_based",
  "payoutConfig": {
    "destinationAccount": "{{destinationAccount}}",
    "destinationBank": "{{destinationBank}}",
    "targetAmount": 10000000
  }
}

exec: pm.test("Request response", () => { throw new Error("Status " + pm.response.code + ": " + pm.response.text()); });

request.description: payoutMode='manual', no fixed destination: an admin picks the destination at the moment they trigger POST /pots/:id/payout, every time — destinationAccount/destinationBank are then REQUIRED in that request's body. See 'Create Pot — Manual (Fixed Destination)' for the alternative where a default is set here instead.

exec: pm.test("Request response", () => { throw new Error("Status " + pm.response.code + ": " + pm.response.text()); });

request.description: payoutMode='manual' with a fixed default destination set at creation (manual_payout_configs) — the triggering admin can still fire it repeatedly, but the destination is pre-agreed and locked in, not chosen per-trigger. POST /pots/:id/payout can then be called with an empty body; any destinationAccount/destinationBank sent there is ignored in favor of this fixed one.

exec: pm.test("Request response", () => { throw new Error("Status " + pm.response.code + ": " + pm.response.text()); });

request.description: payoutMode='recurring': fixed amount sent to one destination every intervalDays, starting at nextRunAt.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Monthly Savings Club",
  "description": "Recurring payout on a fixed interval",
  "potType": "private",
  "refundType": "contributors",
  "minContribution": 100000,
  "payoutMode": "recurring",
  "payoutConfig": {
    "destinationAccount": "{{destinationAccount}}",
    "destinationBank": "{{destinationBank}}",
    "amount": 5000000,
    "intervalDays": 30,
    "nextRunAt": "2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z"
  }
}

exec: pm.test("Request response", () => { throw new Error("Status " + pm.response.code + ": " + pm.response.text()); });

request.description: payoutMode='scheduled', ordered=true: each leg pays out a different destination in sequenceOrder on its own scheduledDate, strictly in turn — classic Ajo/esusu rotation.

exec: pm.test("Request response", () => { throw new Error("Status " + pm.response.code + ": " + pm.response.text()); });

item.description: Run whichever variant matches what you're testing — each sets {{potId}} on success, which every other request in this folder relies on.

request.description: Public pots always included; private pots only included if the bearer token belongs to a member. Works fully unauthenticated too (public pots only) since this route uses optionalAuthenticate.
404 if the pot doesn't exist or is private and the caller isn't a member. optionalAuthenticate — works without a token for public pots.

Admin-only. Only works while the pot is still status='draft' — activate() locks the config in. Can update title/description/potType/refundType/min-maxContribution/goalAmount/payoutMode/payoutConfig together or independently. goalAmount is a display-only fundraising goal available on any payout mode — distinct from target_based's own targetAmount, which actually fires the payout.
Admin-only. Transitions draft -> open, after which contributions can be made and the payout config is locked.

Any authenticated caller can contribute to an 'open' pot (private pots also require membership, enforced same as GET /pots/:id). Returns a pending virtual-account funding intent — the ledger only updates once Nomba's funding webhook confirms the transfer landed. Requires Idempotency-Key header (auto-filled with {{$guid}}). For refundType='contributors' pots, also pass refundAccountNumber/refundBankCode.

item.name: Contribute to Pot — Anonymous, No Auth

request.description: A public pot accepts a contribution with NO bearer token at all — contributorUserId is stored null. Only works against a public pot (a private pot 404s an unauthenticated caller, same visibility rule as GET /pots/:id). For refundType='contributors' pots, refundAccountNumber/refundBankCode are still required here since there's no user profile to fall back on.

Admin-only. Sends a 6-digit confirmation code to the requesting admin's email, required before Trigger Payout will execute. Body must be the SAME destinationAccount/destinationBank/amount (if any) you intend to pass to Trigger Payout — the code is bound to this exact context and won't verify against a different one. Responds 200 { message }.

Admin-only, idempotent per Idempotency-Key. destinationAccount/destinationBank in this body are ONLY read for payoutMode='manual' pots that were created WITHOUT a fixed destination (see 'Create Pot — Manual' vs 'Create Pot — Manual (Fixed Destination)') — omit them entirely for target_based/recurring/scheduled pots, and for a manual pot that already has a fixed destination (this body is ignored in that case, not merged). amount is also manual-only and optional: omit it to disburse the pot's FULL current balance (original behavior); set it for a PARTIAL payout, leaving the rest in the pot — must be >0 and <= the pot's current balance. otpCode is required — call Request Payout OTP first with this SAME destination/amount and paste the emailed code here; it won't verify against a different destination/amount. Responds 202 with no body: the transfer is only ENQUEUED here, not completed — the actual Nomba call and ledger posting happen later in a background worker once the queued job is processed.

Manual mode only. Sends amount instead of the pot's full balance — must be >0 and <= the pot's current balance (409 if it exceeds it). Leaves the remainder in the pot for a later trigger. otpCode must come from a Request Payout OTP call made with this SAME destination/amount.

exec: pm.test("Partial payout accepted for processing (202)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(202));

request.description: Admin-only. Sends a 6-digit confirmation code to the requesting admin's email, required before Trigger Refund will execute. No body. Responds 200 { message }.

Admin-only, idempotent per Idempotency-Key. Drains the pot's full ledger balance — one leg for refundType='admin' (to the admin's refund profile account) or one per contributor for refundType='contributors'. otpCode is required — call Request Refund OTP first and paste the emailed code here. Responds 202 with no body: every leg is only ENQUEUED here, not completed — the actual Nomba call(s) and ledger posting happen later in a background worker.
Admin-only. Requires the pot's ledger balance to be exactly zero (i.e. fully paid out or refunded first) — otherwise expect a 409/422 from PotError.
Same visibility rule as GET /pots/:id — 404 for a private pot the caller can't view.
Admin-only invite. role: 'admin' | 'member' (defaults to 'member' server-side if omitted). Run the Member User register/verify flow first so {{memberUserId}} is populated.

exec: pm.test("Add member response", () => { throw new Error("Status " + pm.response.code + ": " + pm.response.text()); });

request.description: Admin-only. Refuses to demote the pot's last remaining admin.
Admin-only. Refuses to remove the pot's last remaining admin.

item.description: All mutating routes require a Bearer access token (collection-level auth). Money-moving routes (contribute/payout/refund) additionally require an Idempotency-Key header — pre-filled with Postman's {{$guid}} dynamic variable so retries within the same send get a fresh key; re-send the exact same request twice manually if you want to test idempotency (Postman won't reuse the guid across sends).

item.name: Nomba Webhook (not directly testable via Postman)

request.description: This endpoint verifies an HMAC signature computed from NOMBA_WEBHOOK_SECRET over specific parsed fields (see NombaClient.handleWebhook) — Postman can't reproduce that without a pre-request script that duplicates Nomba's exact signing algorithm and your real webhook secret. Left here as a placeholder: either (a) trigger it for real via Nomba's sandbox dashboard against a tunnel (ngrok/etc.) to this route, or (b) write a pre-request script using the secret from your .env once you confirm the exact signing scheme in nomba.client.ts. Sending this request as-is will get a 401.
